'''''Licorice Pizza''''' is a 2021 American [[coming-of-age story|coming-of-age]] [[comedy drama]] film written, produced, shot and directed by [[Paul Thomas Anderson]]. It stars [[Alana Haim]] and [[Cooper Hoffman]] in their film debuts, alongside an ensemble supporting cast including [[Sean Penn]], [[Tom Waits]], [[Bradley Cooper]], and [[Benny Safdie]]. Set in 1973, the film follows the relationship between a teenage actor (Hoffman) and a young woman (Haim).

The film was released in the United States in select theaters on November 26, 2021, followed by a wide release on December 25.<ref name="ReleaseDate">{{cite news|last=Bubp|first=Ashley|date=April 20, 2021|title=Paul Thomas Anderson's Latest Film Announces Holiday Release Date|work=[[Collider (website)|Collider]]|url=https://collider.com/paul-thomas-anderson-new-movie-release-date-2/|access-date=April 21, 2021|archive-date=April 21, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210421073809/https://collider.com/paul-thomas-anderson-new-movie-release-date-2/|url-status=live}}</ref> Though it grossed $33.3 million against its $40 million production budget, the film was acclaimed by critics and received three nominations at the [[94th Academy Awards]]: [[Academy Award for Best Picture|Best Picture]], [[Academy Award for Best Director|Best Director]], and [[Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay|Best Original Screenplay]], making it [[Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer]]'s first fully produced, marketed, and distributed film to be nominated for Best Picture since ''[[Rain Man]]'' in [[61st Academy Awards|1988]].<ref>{{cite web |author-first1=Nancy |author-last1=Tartaglione |url=https://deadline.com/2022/02/mgm-future-oscars-michael-de-luca-pam-abdy-interview-1234929534/ |title=MGM's Michael De Luca & Pam Abdy On Studio's First In-House Best Picture Oscar Nomination In 33 Years, Being "Mildly Psychotically Obsessive" About Movies & What's Ahead – Q&A |work=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |date=February 9, 2022 |access-date=February 26, 2022 |archive-date=February 9, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220209232052/https://deadline.com/2022/02/mgm-future-oscars-michael-de-luca-pam-abdy-interview-1234929534/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Among its many other [[List of accolades received by Licorice Pizza|nominations and awards]], it received three awards from the [[National Board of Review]] (including [[National Board of Review Award for Best Film|Best Film]]), was named one of the best films of 2021 by the [[American Film Institute Awards|American Film Institute]], received four nominations at the [[79th Golden Globe Awards]] (including [[Golden Globe Award for Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy|Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy]]), and won the [[BAFTA Award for Best Original Screenplay]].

==Plot==
<!--Plot summaries should be 400 to 700 words.-->
In 1973 [[San Fernando Valley]], 15-year-old actor Gary Valentine meets 25-year-old Alana Kane, a photographer's assistant, at his school picture day. She is put off by his invitation to dinner, but shows up anyway.

When Gary's mother cannot chaperone him on a press tour performance in New York City, he invites Alana. He is jealous when Alana begins dating his co-star Lance, but they break up after Lance reveals he is an atheist during [[Shabbat]] dinner with her Jewish family. Gary begins selling [[waterbed]]s and reconnects with Alana at a teenage trade expo. Mistaken for a murder suspect, Gary is arrested and Alana runs after him to the police station, but he is soon released.

Alana joins Gary's waterbed business, acting seductively on the phone to land a potential customer. Introducing her to his talent agent, he is upset that she is open to nudity but refuses to show him her breasts. She impulsively does so, but slaps him when he asks to touch them. They open a "Fat Bernie's" storefront for their waterbeds, and Alana is hurt when Gary flirts with his classmate Sue. Peeking in on them making out in the back room, Alana kisses a man on the street before storming off back home.

Gary's agent secures an audition for Alana for a film starring veteran actor Jack Holden, who takes her to the Tail o' the Cock restaurant, where Gary and his friends are also dining. An intoxicated Alana makes Gary jealous, and Holden's friend, film director Rex Blau, convinces him to recreate one of his motorcycle stunts on a nearby golf course, bringing the entire restaurant along. Alana topples off the bike before Holden jumps over a flaming sand trap, and Gary runs to her side. Reconciled, they walk to the waterbed store, where Gary stops himself from touching a sleeping Alana's breast.

The [[1973 oil crisis]] sweeps the country, forcing the waterbed manufacturer to close. Alana, Gary, and his friends make one final delivery to the home of [[Jon Peters]], who humiliates Gary before leaving to meet his girlfriend, [[Barbra Streisand]]. Filling up the waterbed inside, Gary intentionally leaves the hose running, with Alana's approval. They drive away but are waved down by an agitated Peters, whose car has run out of gas, and leave him at a crowded gas station when he violently commandeers a gas pump. Gary stops to smash Peters's car, but runs out of gas as well. Alana maneuvers their truck backward down a long hill to a gas station, impressing Gary, but causing her to question her recent decisions.

Inspired by a campaign poster, Alana reaches out to her old classmate Brian, who brings her on as volunteer staffer for [[Joel Wachs]], a city councilman [[1973 Los Angeles mayoral election|running for mayor]]. Gary briefly joins her but overhears that [[pinball]] will soon be legalized in the Valley and decides to open an [[Amusement arcade|arcade]], leading to an argument with Alana about their difference in age and their fraught relationship. Emasculating Gary to make herself feel superior, Alana offers to drive him home in an attempt to make peace, but Gary drives off alone.

Later, Gary prepares for the opening night of his arcade, remodeling his storefront into "Fat Bernie's Pinball Palace." That same night, Alana nearly shares a kiss with Brian, but is interrupted by an invitation from Wachs. Thinking it is a date, she is dejected to discover Wachs wants her to pose as the girlfriend of his secret boyfriend, Matthew, to save him from political embarrassment.

Alana walks a deeply hurt Matthew home, and they commiserate over the men in their lives. She goes to the arcade to find Gary, who has left to look for her at Wachs's office, with her sisters' encouragement. They eventually run to each other's arms and return to the arcade, where Gary announces her as "Mrs. Alana Valentine." Sharing a kiss, they run into the night, and Alana tells Gary that she loves him.

==Production==
===Development===
[[File:Paul Thomas Anderson 2007 crop.jpg|thumb|left|upright|Writer, director, and producer [[Paul Thomas Anderson]].]]

Around 2001, [[Paul Thomas Anderson]] was walking by a middle school in [[Los Angeles]] on picture day. He observed one of the students nagging the female photographer and had an idea of the student having a romantic relationship with the photographer. The screenplay of ''Licorice Pizza'' evolved from this experience and additional stories told to Anderson by his friend [[Gary Goetzman]], who was a child actor who had starred in the film ''[[Yours, Mine and Ours (1968 film)|Yours, Mine and Ours]]'' with [[Lucille Ball]], appeared on ''[[The Ed Sullivan Show]]'', and eventually started a [[waterbed]] company and [[pinball]] [[Amusement arcade|arcade]]. Goetzman at one time delivered a waterbed to [[Jon Peters]]'s home.<ref>{{cite interview|last=Mankiewicz|first=Ben|author-link=Ben Mankiewicz|url=https://m.youtube.com/watch?v=TKrZfBix-Ns|title=Licorice Pizza Panel/w Paul Thomas Anderson and Alana Haim|time=2:00–4:00, 17:00–18:00, 32:00–33:00|date=November 6, 2021|access-date=November 7, 2021|via=[[YouTube]]|archive-date=November 7, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211107212402/https://www.youtube.com/watch?app=desktop&v=TKrZfBix-Ns|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=LAT211126>{{cite web|last=Whipp|first=Glenn|title=Paul Thomas Anderson's hilarious and intimate 'Licorice Pizza' tour of the Valley|url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment-arts/movies/story/2021-11-26/paul-thomas-anderson-licorice-pizza-san-fernando-valley|website=[[Los Angeles Times]]|access-date=December 11, 2021|date=November 26, 2021|archive-date=December 6, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211206162347/https://www.latimes.com/entertainment-arts/movies/story/2021-11-26/paul-thomas-anderson-licorice-pizza-san-fernando-valley|url-status=live}}</ref> Anderson considered ''[[Fast Times at Ridgemont High]]'' and ''[[American Graffiti]]'' as major influences in the making of ''Licorice Pizza''.<ref name="Variety"/>

Anderson received permission from Jon Peters to develop a character based on him, on the sole condition that Peters's favorite [[pick-up line]] ("Do you like peanut butter sandwiches?"<ref name="ScreenRant/licorice-pizza-facts">{{cite web |last1=Barker |first1=Stephen |title=10 Behind-The-Scenes Facts About Licorice Pizza |url=https://screenrant.com/licorice-pizza-behind-scenes-facts/ |website=ScreenRant |access-date=11 February 2026 |language=en |date=20 February 2022}}</ref>) was used, and Anderson went on to create a "monster version" of Peters based on 1970s Hollywood producers who had "a reputation for a lot of bravado and aggro energy."<ref name="Variety"/>

In September 2021, the film was officially titled ''Licorice Pizza'',<ref name="Shanfeld">{{Cite web |last=Shanfeld |first=Ethan |date=2021-09-27 |title=‘Licorice Pizza’ Trailer: Bradley Cooper Stars in Paul Thomas Anderson’s Coming-of-Age Movie |url=https://variety.com/2021/film/news/paul-thomas-anderson-licorice-pizza-trailer-bradley-cooper-1235046675/ |access-date=2025-11-10 |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]}}</ref> named after [[Licorice Pizza (store)|a former chain of record shops]] in southern California.<ref>{{cite news|last=Nichols|first=Chris|title=A Look Back at Licorice Pizza, the SoCal Record Store P.T. Anderson's New Movie Is Named After|url=https://www.lamag.com/culturefiles/licorice-pizza-paul-thomas-anderson/|access-date=October 4, 2021|work=[[Los Angeles (magazine)|Los Angeles Magazine]]|date=September 15, 2021|archive-date=October 4, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211004153318/https://www.lamag.com/culturefiles/licorice-pizza-paul-thomas-anderson/?utm_campaign=Daily%20Update&utm_medium=email&_hsmi=160046025&_hsenc=p2ANqtz--PiIt7towKm3Vwn24Ps6zD7gl2SgigAwqakdB-APnj79xRyWb_4VeBQ5kPMo1H7dA2XAYOisn-l4SPFXJAwJouH9uDqw&utm_content=160046025&utm_source=hs_email|url-status=live}}</ref> Anderson explained: "If there's two words that make me kind of have a [[Pavlovian response]] and memory of being a child and running around, it's 'licorice' and 'pizza' [...] It instantly takes me back to that time." He added that the words "seemed like a catch-all for the feeling of the film [...] that go well together and maybe capture a mood."<ref name="Variety"/><ref name=LAT211126/>

===Casting===
[[File:Alana Haim during an interview, March 2022.jpg|thumb|right|upright|Alana Haim plays the lead role of Alana Kane, in her film debut.]]
Anderson wrote the screenplay with [[Alana Haim]] in mind and offered her the lead role in summer 2019.<ref name=THR211211>{{cite web|last=Verhoeven|first=Beatrice|title='Licorice Pizza' Star Alana Haim Calls Paul Thomas Anderson Her Biggest Supporter|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-features/alana-haim-interview-licorice-pizza-paul-thomas-anderson-1235054951/|website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|access-date=December 11, 2021|date=December 6, 2021|archive-date=December 9, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211209043717/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-features/alana-haim-interview-licorice-pizza-paul-thomas-anderson-1235054951/|url-status=live}}</ref> He has a close connection to her band [[Haim (band)|Haim]], having directed several of their music videos, and is a close friend of the Haim family.<ref name=NYT211206>{{cite news|last=Zoladz|first=Lindsay|title=Alana Haim Surprised Everyone With Her Movie Debut. Even Herself.|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/12/06/movies/alana-haim-licorice-pizza.html|work=[[The New York Times]]|access-date=December 11, 2021|date=December 6, 2021|archive-date=December 9, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211209182239/https://www.nytimes.com/2021/12/06/movies/alana-haim-licorice-pizza.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Haim's sisters [[Este Haim|Este]] and [[Danielle Haim|Danielle]] and parents [[Mordechai Haim|Mordechai]] and Donna were also cast to play her character's family.<ref name=RS211209>{{cite magazine|last=Greene|first=Andy|title=Re-Introducing Alana Haim, the Knock-Down, Drag-Out Star of 'Licorice Pizza'|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/movies/movie-features/licorice-pizza-alana-haim-p-t-anderson-1268796/|magazine=[[Rolling Stone]]|access-date=December 11, 2021|date=December 9, 2021|archive-date=December 10, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211210204226/https://www.rollingstone.com/movies/movie-features/licorice-pizza-alana-haim-p-t-anderson-1268796/|url-status=live}}</ref> [[Cooper Hoffman]], the son of [[Philip Seymour Hoffman]], was cast late in the process after Anderson found the young actors auditioning to be too "precocious" and "trained" to match the naturalistic style of Haim's acting.<ref name=NYT211206/> ''Licorice Pizza'' marks the feature film debut of both Haim and Hoffman.<ref name=RS211209/><ref name=NYT211122>{{cite news|last=Buchanan|first=Kyle|title=Paul Thomas Anderson Goes Back to the Valley With 'Licorice Pizza'|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/11/22/movies/paul-thomas-anderson-licorice-pizza.html|website=[[The New York Times]]|access-date=December 11, 2021|date=November 22, 2021|archive-date=December 11, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211211002125/https://www.nytimes.com/2021/11/22/movies/paul-thomas-anderson-licorice-pizza.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Described as a "family-and-friends project" by the ''[[Los Angeles Times]]'', the film also features Anderson's longtime partner [[Maya Rudolph]], their four children, and many of their neighborhood friends in various roles.<ref name=LAT211126/>

===Filming===
Principal photography began in [[Encino, Los Angeles|Encino, California]], in August 2020,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://thefilmstage.com/paul-thomas-anderson-begins-shooting-next-film-with-working-title-of-soggy-bottom/|title=Paul Thomas Anderson Begins Shooting Next Film with Working Title of Soggy Bottom|website=The Film Stage|first=Jordan|last=Raup|date=August 24, 2020|access-date=August 24, 2020|archive-date=August 25, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200825005359/https://thefilmstage.com/paul-thomas-anderson-begins-shooting-next-film-with-working-title-of-soggy-bottom/|url-status=live}}</ref> under the [[working title]] ''Soggy Bottom''<ref>{{cite web|last=Welk|first=Brian|date=November 10, 2020|title=Los Angeles Film Shoots at 47% of Pre-COVID Levels, FilmLA Says|url=https://www.thewrap.com/los-angeles-film-shoots-at-47-of-pre-covid-conditions-filmla-says/|url-status=live|access-date=April 21, 2021|website=[[TheWrap]]|archive-date=January 25, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210125101613/https://www.thewrap.com/los-angeles-film-shoots-at-47-of-pre-covid-conditions-filmla-says/}}</ref> which, in the film, is the initial name of Gary's waterbed business. In November 2020, it was reported that principal photography had wrapped and post-production had begun.<ref name="productionwrap">{{cite web|last=Raup|first=Jordan|date=November 19, 2020|title=Paul Thomas Anderson's Soggy Bottom Wraps Filming|url=https://thefilmstage.com/paul-thomas-andersons-soggy-bottom-wraps-filming/|url-status=live|access-date=April 21, 2021|website=The Film Stage|archive-date=January 27, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210127180030/https://thefilmstage.com/paul-thomas-andersons-soggy-bottom-wraps-filming/}}</ref> A [[Tudor Revival]] manor previously owned by actor [[Lyle Waggoner]] was used for scenes at Jon Peters's house.<ref name=Thrillist>{{cite web |last1=Zuckerman |first1=Esther |title=Why Paul Thomas Anderson Chose to Film Part of 'Licorice Pizza' at My Childhood Home |url=https://www.thrillist.com/paul-thomas-anderson-interview-licorice-pizza-movie |website=[[Thrillist]] |access-date=December 12, 2021 |date=November 24, 2021 |archive-date=December 12, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211212210111/https://www.thrillist.com/paul-thomas-anderson-interview-licorice-pizza-movie |url-status=live }}</ref> Tail o' the Cock, a local restaurant that was demolished in 1987, was recreated for the film at the [[Van Nuys]] Golf Course.<ref name=LAT211126/><ref name=LADN>{{cite web|title=Recognize these San Fernando Valley sites? Enjoy these glimpses of some 'Licorice Pizza' locations|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2021/12/10/recognize-these-san-fernando-valley-sites-enjoy-these-glimpses-of-some-licorice-pizza-locations/|website=[[Los Angeles Daily News]]|access-date=December 11, 2021|date=December 10, 2021|archive-date=December 10, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211210232427/https://www.dailynews.com/2021/12/10/recognize-these-san-fernando-valley-sites-enjoy-these-glimpses-of-some-licorice-pizza-locations/|url-status=live}}</ref> Haim spent a week learning to drive large trucks, and personally performed the stunt where her character backs the truck down a long hill.<ref name=THR211211/>

Anderson and [[Michael Bauman (cinematographer)|Michael Bauman]] (sharing a director of photography credit) shot ''Licorice Pizza'' on [[35 mm movie film|35 mm film]], using older lenses in order to create the film's 1970s texture.<ref name=Deadline>{{cite web|last=Topel|first=Fred|title='Licorice Pizza' Used '70s Film Tech to Tell A '70s Love Story – Contenders L.A.|url=https://deadline.com/2021/11/licorice-pizza-michael-bauman-andy-jurgensen-florencia-martin-contenders-los-angeles-1234872594/|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|access-date=December 11, 2021|date=November 14, 2021|archive-date=December 5, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211205015153/https://deadline.com/2021/11/licorice-pizza-michael-bauman-andy-jurgensen-florencia-martin-contenders-los-angeles-1234872594/|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Music===
{{Main|Licorice Pizza (soundtrack){{!}} ''Licorice Pizza'' (soundtrack)}}
[[Radiohead]]'s [[Jonny Greenwood]] composed the film's score cues. The first trailer for the film, which was released online on September 27, 2021, was set to [[David Bowie]]'s "[[Life on Mars (song)|Life on Mars?]],"<ref>{{cite web|last=Goslin|first=Austen|url=https://www.polygon.com/22696464/licorice-pizza-trailer-pta-cooper-hoffman-alana-haim|title=The Licorice Pizza trailer prepares us for Paul Thomas Anderson's good vibes event film|work=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]]|date=September 27, 2021|access-date=September 27, 2021|archive-date=September 27, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210927203808/https://www.polygon.com/22696464/licorice-pizza-trailer-pta-cooper-hoffman-alana-haim|url-status=live}}</ref> which also is featured in the film.

The film's official soundtrack was released by [[Republic Records]]. Included are many of the period songs featured in the film, as well as one of the original tracks composed by Greenwood.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://filmmusicreporter.com/|title='Licorice Pizza' Soundtrack Album Details|work=Field Music Reporter|date=November 9, 2021|access-date=November 9, 2021|archive-date=October 27, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211027182450/http://filmmusicreporter.com/|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Release==
In December 2019, [[Focus Features]], which had financed and released Anderson's previous film ''[[Phantom Thread]]'', came on to produce and distribute the film.<ref name="PTAFocusfilm">{{cite magazine|first=Rebecca|last=Rubin|title=Paul Thomas Anderson's Next Film Lands at Focus Features|url=https://variety.com/2019/film/news/paul-thomas-anderson-film-focus-features-1203447479/|date=December 18, 2019|magazine=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|access-date=March 3, 2020|archive-date=April 8, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200408023101/https://variety.com/2019/film/news/paul-thomas-anderson-film-focus-features-1203447479/|url-status=live}}</ref> However, in July 2020, it was reported that [[Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer]] had agreed to co-produce the film, and acquired the distribution rights from Focus, presumably due to budgetary issues, and that MGM would set a new start date due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref name="PTA&MGM">{{cite magazine|first=Borys|last=Kit|title=Paul Thomas Anderson's 1970s High School Movie Moving From Focus to MGM|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/paul-thomas-andersons-1970s-high-school-movie-moving-focus-mgm-1303665|date=July 17, 2020|magazine=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|access-date=July 19, 2020|archive-date=September 16, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200916192124/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/paul-thomas-andersons-1970s-high-school-movie-moving-focus-mgm-1303665|url-status=live}}</ref> In September 2021, the film's trailer and title were revealed at screenings of ''American Graffiti'' in London and in Los Angeles, before being released later that same month.<ref name="Shanfeld" />

The film was [[limited theatrical release|released in select theaters]] in the United States by [[United Artists Releasing]] on November 26, 2021, followed by a nationwide release on December 25, 2021. It was released in the [[United Kingdom]] on January 14, 2022, by [[Universal Pictures]].<ref name="ReleaseDate" /><ref>{{cite web|last=Raup|first=Jordan|date=April 20, 2021|title=Paul Thomas Anderson's Next Film Set for Fall 2021 Release|url=https://thefilmstage.com/paul-thomas-andersons-next-film-set-for-christmas-day-release/|url-status=live|access-date=April 21, 2021|website=The Film Stage|archive-date=April 20, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210420195526/https://thefilmstage.com/paul-thomas-andersons-next-film-set-for-christmas-day-release/}}</ref>

===Home media===
[[Universal Pictures Home Entertainment]] released the film digitally on March 1, 2022, and on both [[Blu-ray]] and [[DVD]] on May 17.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.blu-ray.com/Licorice-Pizza/1423999/|title=Licorice Pizza (2021)|access-date=March 30, 2022|archive-date=March 30, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220330083324/https://www.blu-ray.com/Licorice-Pizza/1423999/|url-status=live}}</ref>
==Reception==
===Box office===
''Licorice Pizza'' grossed $17.3 million in the United States and Canada, and $15.9 million in other territories, for a worldwide box office total of $33.2 million.<ref name="BOM"/><ref name="NUM"/> ''[[Deadline Hollywood]]'' reported the film lost money for the studio, though did note it "brought a pulse to arthouses during a downbeat time."<ref>{{cite web |last1=D'Alessandro |first1=Anthony |title='Super Mario Bros' Has Best Third Weekend For Animated Pic With $58M+; 'Evil Dead Rise' Still Alive With $23M+ – Sunday Box Office Update |url=https://deadline.com/2023/04/box-office-evil-dead-rise-super-mario-bros-movie-2-1235333373/ |website=Deadline Hollywood |date=April 22, 2023 |access-date=April 23, 2023 |archive-date=May 22, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230522142257/https://deadline.com/2023/04/box-office-evil-dead-rise-super-mario-bros-movie-2-1235333373/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

The film opened in four theaters on November 26, 2021, including the [[Regency Village Theatre]] in Los Angeles. It made $335,000 its opening weekend, for an average of $83,800 per screen.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2021/11/licorice-pizza-paul-thomas-anderson-thanksgiving-indie-box-office-1234881070/|title='Licorice Pizza' Delivers: Paul Thomas Anderson Pic's Opening Among Filmmaker's Best With Record Screen Average – Specialty Box Office|date=November 28, 2021|first=Anthony|last=D'Alessandro|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|access-date=November 28, 2021|archive-date=November 28, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211128194419/https://deadline.com/2021/11/licorice-pizza-paul-thomas-anderson-thanksgiving-indie-box-office-1234881070/|url-status=live}}</ref>

Its fifth weekend, the film expanded to 786 theaters and entered the box office top ten for the first time with $1.9 million, finishing eighth. During the weekend, 66% of audience members were between the ages of 18 and 34.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.boxofficemojo.com/weekend/2021W52/|title=Domestic 2021 Weekend 52|website=[[Box Office Mojo]]|access-date=December 30, 2021|archive-date=December 29, ===Critical response===
{{Rotten Tomatoes prose|90|8.3|326|''Licorice Pizza'' finds Paul Thomas Anderson shifting into a surprisingly comfortable gear – and getting potentially star-making performances out of his fresh-faced leads.|ref=yes|access-date=September 14, 2025}} [[Metacritic]], which uses a [[Weighted arithmetic mean|weighted average]], assigned the film a score of 90 out of 100, based on 55 critics, indicating "universal acclaim".<ref name="Metacritic">{{cite web |title=''Licorice Pizza'' |url=https://www.metacritic.com/movie/licorice-pizza |website=[[Metacritic]] |publisher=[[Fandom (website)#Fandom, Inc.|Fandom, Inc.]] |access-date= |archive-url= |archive-date= |url-status=}}</ref><ref>{{cite Metacritic|id=licorice-pizza|type=movie|title=Licorice Pizza|access-date=January 11, 2022}}{{cbignore}}</ref> Audiences polled by [[PostTrak]] gave the film an 87% positive score, with 73% saying they would definitely recommend it.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2021/11/encanto-house-of-gucci-resident-evil-thanksgiving-box-office-1234880192/|title=The Sobering Reality Of Thanksgiving Box Office During Pandemic With 'Encanto' Sans 'Top Gun 2'; Adults Return For 'House Of Gucci', 'Licorice Pizza'|date=November 27, 2021|first=Anthony|last=D'Alessandro|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|access-date=November 28, 2021|archive-date=November 25, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211125222254/https://deadline.com/2021/11/encanto-house-of-gucci-resident-evil-thanksgiving-box-office-1234880192/|url-status=live}}</ref> In June 2025, ''[[IndieWire]]'' ranked the film at number 35 on its list of "The 100 Best Movies of the 2020s (So Far)."<ref>{{cite web |date=June 16, 2025 |title=The 100 Best Movies of the 2020s (So Far) |url=https://www.indiewire.com/lists/best-movies-2020s/ |access-date=June 23, 2025 |archive-date=July 27, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250727024924/https://www.indiewire.com/lists/best-movies-2020s/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Accolades===
{{Main|List of accolades received by Licorice Pizza {{!}} List of accolades received by ''Licorice Pizza''}}
''Licorice Pizza'' was nominated in three categories at the [[94th Academy Awards]] ([[Academy Award for Best Picture|Best Picture]], [[Academy Award for Best Director|Best Director]], and [[Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay|Best Original Screenplay]]), in four at the [[79th Golden Globe Awards]] ([[Golden Globe Award for Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy|Best Picture – Musical or Comedy]], [[Golden Globe Award for Best Actor – Motion Picture Musical or Comedy|Best Actor – Musical or Comedy]], [[Golden Globe Award for Best Actress – Motion Picture Comedy or Musical|Best Actress – Musical or Comedy]], and [[Golden Globe Award for Best Screenplay|Best Screenplay]]), and in five at the [[75th British Academy Film Awards]] ([[BAFTA Award for Best Film|Best Film]], [[BAFTA Award for Best Actress in a Leading Role|Best Actress]], [[BAFTA Award for Best Direction|Best Director]], [[BAFTA Award for Best Original Screenplay|Best Original Screenplay]], and [[BAFTA Award for Best Editing|Best Editing]]), with Paul Thomas Anderson winning Original Screenplay. The film was ranked second on ''[[Cahiers du Cinéma]]''{{'}}s list of the top 10 films of 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.indiewire.com/2022/12/cahiers-du-cinema-best-films-of-2022-list-1234787270/|website=[[IndieWire]]|title='Pacifiction' Tops Cahiers du Cinema's Best Films of 2022 List|first=Christian|last=Zilko|date=December 1, 2022|access-date=December 5, 2022|archive-date=December 6, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221206111408/https://www.indiewire.com/2022/12/cahiers-du-cinema-best-films-of-2022-list-1234787270/|url-status=live}}</ref>
